free_tier.stated: US/EU: Storage-0.5TB 500 GB, Storage-1 1 TB, Storage-2 2 TB (SATA RAID-10, 10 Gbps port). APAC: same three sizes in Tokyo and Singapore but with a quarter of the bandwidth. **No plan above 2 TB exists.**
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Metered annual-bundled allowance, no published overage rate. US/EU: 0.5 TB->3 TB, 1 TB->6 TB, 2 TB->10 TB per month. APAC: 0.5 TB->1 TB, 1 TB->2 TB, 2 TB->4 TB. I.e. APAC is 1/2.5 of the US figure. This is the Asia option's real trap: the Tokyo/Singapore plans cost the same as US/EU and give 40% of the traffic.

chaining: Root KVM on a 10 Gbps port, which is unusually fast for this price class. Ceiling of 2 TB per VM means 10 VMs for 20 TB. Workable for the chunk-and-replicate pattern but not for a single 10 TiB working set.
limits_note: per-object-cap: none. Hard 2 TB per-VM ceiling. APAC bandwidth 40% of US/EU.
reliability_note: Established hosting provider with positive community reviews for storage VPS lines and active hosting thread presence.
